title.quote: Implicit meta-learning may lead language models to trust more reliable sources
title.justification: Title as given at the top of the paper.
title.value: Implicit meta-learning may lead language models to trust more reliable sources

extractions.description: The paper studies "implicit meta-learning" (IML): language models fine-tuned on synthetic data containing random-string "define tags" that indicate source reliability later internalize statements from the reliable-seeming source more. Experiments include two-stage fine-tuning of Pythia, GPT-Neo, Llama2 and T5 models on CVDB- and T-REx-derived QA datasets, a toy set-inclusion task training Pythia-70M from scratch, an MNIST-based vision task with ConvNeXt V2, gradient-alignment measurements, and linear probing.

type.quote: We perform a thorough empirical investigation of this phenomenon
type.justification: The paper is an empirical investigation with many fine-tuning experiments and ablations.
